title: Cost to Tile a Bathroom in 2026
description: See what it costs to tile a bathroom floor and shower in 2026, with per square foot prices, a full worked budget, and ways to save.

cover.alt: A small bathroom being tiled, with gray floor tiles and white wall tiles going in and a tile saw nearby

tool.name: Tile calculator
tool.short: Tiles and boxes for any tile size

takeaways: Angi puts the average cost to retile a bathroom at $2,000, with most jobs from $450 to $8,000.
Bathroom tile runs $10 to $50 per square foot installed, based on Angi 2026 data.
Shower tile costs more per foot than floor tile, because of waterproofing and cuts.
body:
Angi's 2026 data puts the average cost to retile a bathroom at $2,000, and most homeowners pay between $450 and $8,000. Per square foot, plan on $10 to $50 installed for bathroom tile. A floor only job sits at the low end, and a full shower with stone tile sits at the high end.

## What does it cost to tile a bathroom in 2026?

HomeGuide lists a bathroom floor at 40 to 160 sq ft with a total cost of $400 to $8,000, and a shower at $420 to $6,000. HomeGuide also puts shower and bathroom tile at $7 to $25 per square foot for many standard jobs. The wider Angi range, $10 to $50 per square foot, covers premium tile, small rooms, and hard layouts.

| Job | Low | Typical | High |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bathroom floor, 40 sq ft, ceramic | $400 | $800 | $1,500 |
| Bathroom floor and walls, 100 sq ft | $1,000 | $2,400 | $5,000 |
| Tub surround or shower, 70 sq ft | $700 | $1,800 | $3,500 |
| Full retile, floor plus shower, stone tile | $3,000 | $5,500 | $10,000 or more |

Small bathrooms cost more per square foot than large ones. The installer still sets up a saw, mixes thinset, and makes the same trips. A minimum charge spreads over fewer feet, so the per foot price climbs.

Tile choice moves the material bill a lot. Angi lists bathroom tile materials at $7 to $25 per square foot for many products, with ceramic at the low end and natural stone at the high end. Labor adds $3 to $15 per square foot on Angi data, with small tile and patterns at the top of that range.

## Worked example: floor and tub surround in a 5 x 8 ft bathroom

Say you retile a standard bathroom. The floor is 5 x 8 ft, or 40 sq ft. The tub surround has three walls that add up to 70 sq ft of tile. Total tile area is 110 sq ft, and you pick mid range porcelain tile.

Price the job in parts, using rates inside the ranges above.

- Floor tile work: 40 sq ft x $18 per sq ft installed = $720.
- Surround tile work: 70 sq ft x $25 per sq ft installed = $1,750.
- Waterproofing for the wet walls: allow $600 as a flat line.
- Subtotal: $720 + $1,750 + $600 = $3,070.
- Round up for trim, caulk, and disposal: budget $3,200.

Check the total a second way. The full 110 sq ft at a blended rate near $28 per sq ft gives about $3,080, which matches the line item total before rounding. If you do the floor only, the same math gives $720, and most quotes for a floor only job in this size land between $500 and $1,500 once a minimum charge applies.

For a DIY version of this job, you pay for tile, backer board, thinset, and grout only. On this room that is often $600 to $900 in materials, plus a tile saw rental. You save the labor, but the shower waterproofing is the part that must be right. A leak behind tile costs far more than the labor you saved. Use our [tile calculator](/blog/tile-calculator/) for the tile count and our [grout calculator](/blog/grout-calculator/) for grout bags before you price materials.

## What pushes the price up or down?

Demo and prep come first. Pulling old tile, fixing a soft subfloor, or leveling a floor adds $200 to $1,400 on many jobs. A floor that is flat and sound keeps you at the low end.

Tile size and pattern come next. Large format tile, 12 x 24 in or bigger, sets fast on flat walls. Small mosaic sheets, herringbone, and diagonal layouts need more cuts and more time. Fixr notes that elaborate patterns add about 10 to 20 percent to tile floor work, and bathroom quotes follow the same pattern.

Wet area work costs more than dry floor work. A shower needs a pan or sloped base, a waterproof membrane, and sealed changes of plane. That is skilled work with no shortcut. Niches, benches, and glass block or accent strips each add a flat charge.

Your region matters too. Labor is the larger half of most tile quotes, so metro rates run high and rural rates run low. The tile itself ships nationally and varies less.

## DIY or hire a tile pro?

A straight floor in a dry bathroom is a fair DIY job for a careful homeowner. You need a flat subfloor, cement backer board or an uncoupling mat, and time to let thinset cure. Rent a wet saw for porcelain, because a snap cutter chips hard tile.

Hire a pro for a shower or tub surround if you have not built a waterproof system before. Tile and grout are not the waterproof layer. The membrane behind them is, and it has to tie into the drain. Pros also set tile flatter, with fewer lips between tiles that catch toes and collect grime.

If you hire out, get three quotes with the same scope in writing. Each quote should list demo, prep, waterproofing method, tile setting, grout, sealing, and disposal as separate lines. A single lump sum hides the line that will grow later. Our [flooring calculator](/blog/flooring-calculator/) helps you check the floor area a quote is based on.

## How can you save money on bathroom tile?

Keep the layout you have. Moving a drain or a tub adds plumbing cost that dwarfs the tile bill. Tile the floor and the wet walls, and paint the dry walls. Paint is cheap to change later.

Pick a mid range porcelain tile in a standard size. Porcelain wears well, needs no sealing, and costs less than stone to buy and to set. Save the pricey tile for a small accent strip if you want one feature.

Do your own demo if you are able. Pulling tile and hauling debris is hard, dusty work, but it needs no license and it can cut several hundred dollars. Protect the tub with plywood before you start, and shut off water lines to the room.

Buy the tile yourself only if the installer agrees. You gain control of price, but you own the risk of short orders and dye lot changes. Add 10 percent extra for cuts on a straight layout, and 15 percent for diagonal work. Our guide to [laminate vs vinyl plank cost](/blog/laminate-vs-vinyl-plank-cost/) is worth a look if tile quotes push you to weigh a waterproof plank floor for the dry part of the room.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does it cost to tile a 40 square foot bathroom floor?
At $10 to $50 per square foot installed, a 40 sq ft floor runs $400 to $2,000. Most standard ceramic or porcelain floors land at $600 to $1,200, with a minimum charge lifting small jobs.

### How much does it cost to tile a shower?
HomeGuide puts a shower retile at $7 to $25 per square foot, with a typical total of $800 to $3,800 for tile work. Custom pans, niches, and stone tile push a shower to $5,000 or more.

### Is porcelain or ceramic cheaper for a bathroom?
Ceramic is usually cheaper to buy and easier to cut. Porcelain costs a bit more and is denser and harder, so it suits floors and busy family bathrooms. Both beat natural stone on price and upkeep.

### How long does it take to tile a bathroom?
A pro tiles a floor in 1 to 2 days and a full shower in 3 to 5 days, plus cure time. Grout can go in a day after setting, and showers need a few days before use. Ask your installer for the full schedule in writing.

### Do I need to seal bathroom tile and grout?
Porcelain and ceramic tile need no sealer. Cement grout does, and a penetrating sealer is a small cost that slows staining. Natural stone needs sealing on a regular cycle, which is part of its higher upkeep.

## Next step
Measure your floor and walls, run the counts in our [tile calculator](/blog/tile-calculator/), and bring that sheet to your quote visits so every pro prices the same job.

*Prices are US figures from 2026 and vary by region and supplier.*
